Fixed and released 2026-08-26 in Android 7.7.42 (324) and Flutter 1.14.8+142. Per-telco CityDensity is gone: both apps now resolve density from the authoritative geohash_density table by the site's own position, so every carrier gets the same propagation environment for the same place. Measured across Australia before the fix: of 4,838 geohash-5 cells carrying two or more carriers, 498 (10.3%) had carriers assigned DIFFERENT densities - which is exactly this report. Now zero by construction. 129,399 sites all resolve; no cell overlaps another; both apps assert the same reference geohashes. Spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-25-geohash-density-design.md, plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-geohash-density.md, in the Java repo. Note the separate sparse-coefficient half of this report was addressed earlier by the nearest-density fallback (commits 8b3a8b7 / ac4fabfa).

Root cause found and fixed in worktree issue-56-subagents-852854 (uncommitted, awaiting Brad): yearly_adfree is a Consumable in App Store Connect, so Apple resold it and StoreKit restore could never return it. App now scans Transaction.all (SKIncludeConsumableInAppPurchaseHistory), handles revocations, reconciles a stale cache, pops the Settings sheet before the restore snackbar, refuses to resell ad-free, silences restore thank-yous, retries failed ad loads. 314 tests pass.

Not a defect. Confirmed on device 2026-09-09 with the Developer Mode store diagnostics shipped in 1.14.21+156: the footer reports 'Storefront: USA'.

So the app's product query answered from the US storefront (quoting the US price point, $3.99 USD) while the TestFlight purchase sheet was drawn by the Australian Sandbox Apple Account (charging the real A$5.99). Both render a bare '$', which is why it read as one currency with two numbers - $3.99 USD and A$5.99 are the same Apple price point.

Confirms the code audit: every label is ProductDetails.price, which under StoreKit 2 is Apple's Product.displayPrice verbatim, and initiatePurchase buys the same ProductDetails object the label was built from. Nothing in the app invents or mis-maps a price.

Unreachable by customers: the app ships to Australia only, so a real buyer has an AU account and sees A$5.99 in both places. The reporting device is the one machine whose App Store account (US) and Sandbox Apple Account (AU) disagree - fixed by Settings > [name] > Media & Purchases > View Account > Country/Region.

The diagnostics that settled it stay in the app (PR #68): Developer Mode footer on Support the App, plus storefront and currency codes on the products_loaded analytics event.
Flutter coverage behavior, async safety, coefficient compatibility, tests, and documentation are in sync with Android.
